tactics.name: K monotonicity strengthening
tactics.summary: Promote K(new)>=K(old) from a local swap check into a batch-wide safety law and runtime guard.
tactics.trigger: Use when a pool, batch executor, or settlement transformer changes reserves.
tactics.transform: Enforce reserve monotonicity and prefer exact K-gap accounting when the model exposes a remainder law.
obligations: Check K(new)>=K(old) under the admitted fee and reserve domain.
Prefer an exact K-gap law when the batch model exposes one.
failure_modes: Fee semantics diverge from the proof model and K can drop.
Batch accounting keeps only monotonicity and loses the exact K-gap explanation.

tactics.name: Total order canonicalization
tactics.summary: Replace ambiguous maximizers with a total key over objective and tie-break order.
tactics.trigger: Use when a finite candidate set contains multiple equal-objective winners.
tactics.transform: Rank by the primary objective, then a total tie-break, and choose the unique canonical winner.
obligations: Define a total key, not just a stable sort order.
Prove that equal-objective candidates collapse to a unique canonical representative.
failure_modes: Multiple winners remain semantically equivalent but unspecified.
Enumeration order leaks into consensus-critical winner selection.

tactics.name: Equal marginal dualization
tactics.summary: Seed split routing with the equal-marginal law and search only a bounded neighborhood.
tactics.trigger: Use when a parallel-pool exact-in route needs structure stronger than brute force.
tactics.transform: Relax to the continuous CPMM objective, solve the equal-marginal condition, then prune integer candidates around the seed.
obligations: Check strict concavity on the admitted pool domain.
Connect the seed to a bounded discrete certificate before claiming proof-backed optimality.
Check that the integer optimum lies in the bounded candidate envelope.
failure_modes: Continuous seeds are used outside the domain where concavity applies.
A continuous seed is treated as proof-backed without a discrete certificate bridge.
Integer rounding moves the optimum outside the searched envelope.

tactics.name: Anti fragmentation certificate
tactics.summary: Reject same-pool same-direction fragmentation when single execution dominates sequential fragments.
tactics.trigger: Use when a router considers splitting a same-direction trade across the same pool.
tactics.transform: Compare single execution against fragmented execution and prune the fragmented branch when the certificate holds.
obligations: Check that the fragments share the same pool and direction.
Match the pool fee semantics to the zero-fee or fee-aware proof lane before pruning.
failure_modes: Cross-pool fragmentation is pruned as if it were the same-pool case.
The router keeps dominated same-pool fragments in the candidate set.

tactics.name: Zero fee anti fragmentation carry
tactics.summary: For zero-fee same-pool same-direction two-way splits, merged execution equals split execution plus a carry term and the gap is in {0,1}.
tactics.trigger: Use when a zero-fee routing or audit path compares a merged exact-in swap against a same-pool same-direction two-fragment split.
tactics.transform: Replace ad hoc split comparison with the proof-backed carry law, then prune the split when the carry is nonzero and retain gap<=1 as the exact rounding envelope.
obligations: Restrict the slice to zero-fee CPMM semantics and same-pool same-direction two-way splits.
Do not reuse the carry theorem for fee-retaining pools or cross-pool fragmentation without separate proof support.
failure_modes: Fee-aware fragmentation is labeled proof-backed even though only the zero-fee slice is proved.
Multi-fragment same-pool pruning is treated as if the two-way carry theorem applied directly without the batch bound.

tactics.name: Surplus CBC outcome typing
tactics.summary: Make filled-below-min_out unrepresentable by using a proof-carrying outcome type.
tactics.trigger: Use when batch executors or optimizers compare user outcomes against minima.
tactics.transform: Model outcomes as unfilled or filled(output,pf:output>=min_out) before computing surplus.
obligations: Ensure every bridge constructs only valid outcomes.
Keep surplus derived from validated outcomes, not unchecked arithmetic.
failure_modes: Runtime layers can represent filled below min_out as an ordinary state.
Surplus goes negative only because validation was deferred too late.

tactics.name: Unique canonical winner
tactics.summary: Upgrade deterministic winner selection to existence of a unique canonical minimizer or maximizer.
tactics.trigger: Use when a finite candidate set is ranked by a total key.
tactics.transform: Select the unique key minimum instead of keeping multiple equal winners or unstable enumeration order.
obligations: Prove the candidate set is nonempty and the key is total.
Prove uniqueness, not just repeatability of the implementation.
failure_modes: Code is deterministic but the winning object is not uniquely specified.
Different implementations pick different equal-objective winners.

tactics.name: Batch K gap accounting
tactics.summary: Track exact batch K increase as a sum of per-step remainders instead of a bare monotone flag.
tactics.trigger: Use when batch execution or audit tooling needs a precise reserve-growth explanation.
tactics.transform: Expose K(final)=K(init)+sum remainders and attach the remainder ledger to certificates.
obligations: Maintain the same state-transition model across proof and runtime.
Keep per-step state order explicit in the batch ledger.
failure_modes: Batch audit can say K grew but cannot say by how much or why.
A mismatch appears between step order and the remainder decomposition.

tactics.name: LP roundtrip no profit
tactics.summary: Treat deposit then withdraw no-profit as a first-class LP safety barrier.
tactics.trigger: Use when LP mint, burn, or reserve accounting semantics change.
tactics.transform: Require immediate round-trip withdrawals to stay componentwise below or equal to deposits.
obligations: Match runtime mint and burn formulas to the proof model.
Keep reserve and LP supply preconditions explicit.
failure_modes: LP round-trips leak value due to mint or burn asymmetry.
A reserve update changes LP accounting but no round-trip barrier is checked.

tactics.name: Routing tiebreak totalization
tactics.summary: Specify a total tie-break for equal-quality split routes instead of relying on incidental iteration order.
tactics.trigger: Use when many-pool exact-in or exact-out routing returns equal-quality allocations.
tactics.transform: Canonicalize by objective first, then leg count, then sorted leg tuples keyed by pool_id.
obligations: Prove or test full allocation and deterministic leg ordering.
Use the same canonical key in every implementation path.
failure_modes: Equal-quality routes oscillate across implementations or refactors.
A tie-break differs between exact-in and exact-out dispatch layers.

tactics.name: Max legs capacity guard
tactics.summary: Use max-leg capacity as an explicit feasibility contract before exact-out search.
tactics.trigger: Use when exact-out routing must satisfy a target under a max_legs budget.
tactics.transform: Reject infeasible requests early via top-capacity coverage and keep the failure reason canonical.
obligations: Define per-pool output caps precisely.
Show the coverage test matches solver feasibility under max_legs.
failure_modes: Search explores impossible exact-out requests under the leg budget.
Routing fails without a canonical feasibility explanation.

tactics.name: Commutativity quarantine
tactics.summary: Forbid commutative rewrites once settlement directions oppose.
tactics.trigger: Use when an optimizer or canonicalizer wants to reorder mixed-direction settlements.
tactics.transform: Gate reordering behind same-direction preconditions and preserve explicit order otherwise.
obligations: Check that opposite direction implies a positive commutativity gap on the admitted domain.
Reject commutative rewrites when the precondition fails.
failure_modes: A mixed-direction batch is simplified as if it were commutative.
An optimizer prunes the wrong branch after an unsound reorder.

tactics.name: Oracle uncertainty freeze
tactics.summary: Freeze zUSD risky operations until oracle state is fresh, initialized, and pending price matches the active price.
tactics.trigger: Use when a stablecoin path can mutate debt or collateral using oracle-dependent state.
tactics.transform: Gate risky operations behind oracle_seen ∧ price>0 ∧ price_pending>0 ∧ price_pending=price ∧ OracleFresh ∧ ¬RecoveryMode.
obligations: Keep the risky-ops predicate aligned across runtime, Tau integration, and kernel adapters.
Block oracle-sensitive state transitions whenever pending price diverges from active or freshness fails.
failure_modes: Collateral or debt mutates while the pending oracle price disagrees with the active price.
Runtime and Tau layers disagree on when recovery mode or stale data should block risky operations.

tactics.name: Routing allocation contract
tactics.summary: For exact-in, require full input consumption and positive legs; for exact-out, use the audited selected-domain feasibility bridge to require full-output coverage and positive capacity-bounded support legs.
tactics.trigger: Use when a split router returns many-pool exact-in allocations or exact-out allocations on the audited selected-domain CPMM lane.
tactics.transform: Enforce Σ leg inputs = D for exact-in, use the exact-out feasibility/presentation bridge to require Σ leg outputs = Q on the audited selected-domain lane, and keep emitted legs positive and admissible under the proved capacity or runtime min-valid boundary.
obligations: Use the exact-in Lean allocation theorem only for full-input and positive-leg claims.
Use the exact-out audited selected-domain feasibility and support-presentation chain for Σ leg outputs = Q and positive capacity-bounded support legs.
Keep runtime min-valid or non-modeled admissibility checks fail-closed where they are not yet bundled into one promoted theorem.
failure_modes: The exact-out audited selected-domain feasibility bridge is downgraded to contract-only despite existing Lean support.
A returned route leaves part of the requested volume unallocated.
A combined routing claim treats non-modeled runtime admissibility details as already unified into one theorem when only the decomposed proof lane has been discharged.

tactics.name: Exact-out audited bounds contract
tactics.summary: Bind selected-domain, repaired-domain, and full-domain exact-out budgets plus explicit public success/failure outcomes into one fail-closed audited-bounds contract.
tactics.trigger: Use when a many-pool exact-out quote surface spans selected-domain certificates, repaired bounded advisory behavior, and explicit public budget parameters.
tactics.transform: Rebuild budget_facts_ok and public_outcome_explicit from the nested packet family, require max_legs and the rest of the public budget parameters to agree across layers, and reject payload drift unless the audited-bounds contract rebuilds canonically.
obligations: Keep selected-domain, repaired-domain, and full-domain budget facts explicit rather than implicit in nested packet structure.
Bind max_legs and the rest of the public budget parameters across the selected-domain, repaired, and public contract layers.
Do not overclaim this bounded contract shell as a step-count or global generator-completeness theorem.
failure_modes: Nested packet layers disagree on max_legs or other audited budget parameters while the public contract still appears valid.
The public quote surface succeeds without an explicit replayable success branch or an explicit fail-closed rejection branch.
A bounded audited-bounds contract is overclaimed as an actual liveness or completeness proof.

tactics.name: Repaired replacement shadow alignment
tactics.summary: On claimed supported audited corpora, require the current default many-pool exact-out policy to match the repaired replacement and avoid spurious packet failures.
tactics.trigger: Use when auditing whether the bounded default many-pool exact-out policy still lags the repaired replacement on supported non-CPMM curve families.
tactics.transform: Replay the default packet and repaired replacement on the same bounded corpus, require replacement availability and full-canonicality, and treat any shadow/default packet failure or strict replacement case as a regression.
obligations: Keep the corpus parameters explicit: supported three-pool ordered products, bounded amount_out values, and declared candidate budgets.
Require shadow/default packet success and zero strict-replacement cases on the claimed corpus instead of inferring alignment from one witness.
Do not overclaim supported-corpus shadow alignment as global generator completeness or as a guarantee for wider pool-count domains without separate evidence.
failure_modes: The default quote surface returns nothing on the claimed supported corpus even though the repaired replacement is available and full-canonical.
A strict-replacement case reappears on the claimed supported corpus.
Supported-corpus shadow alignment is mistaken for a global completeness theorem.

tactics.name: Hierarchical proof frontier refinement
tactics.summary: Stabilize a proof frontier by forcing a two-level outline, explicit subgoal state, counterexample-first preflight, and declarative landing criteria.
tactics.trigger: Use when a Lean theorem or contract frontier is blocked by scope confusion between a local minimizer theorem and a stronger generator or completeness claim.
tactics.transform: Split the frontier into replayable local theorems plus explicit generator soundness and completeness obligations; explore procedurally, but land only the declarative theorem or contract actually justified.
obligations: Write a two-level outline before tactics.
Record normalized subgoals, candidate lemmas, failure reasons, and the next repair move.
Keep the informal proof idea and scope boundary adjacent to the formal artifact.
failure_modes: Local emitted-domain canonicality is overclaimed as global generator completeness.
Proof search thrashes because failed plans, counterexamples, and scope boundaries are not preserved.

tactics.name: Decompose and symmetrize
tactics.summary: Decompose the object until the pieces are understandable, then exploit whatever transformations leave the problem unchanged.
tactics.trigger: Use when a proof repeats equivalent cases under asset swaps, route reorderings, participant renamings, mirror states, transition kinds, or other symmetry actions.
tactics.transform: Define the quotient or canonicalization map, prove coverage and no-loss/transfer lemmas, then prove the property for canonical representatives or transition kinds instead of every concrete case.
obligations: Define an explicit abstraction or quotient map from concrete states to canonical representatives.
Prove coverage: every concrete state maps to a canonical representative.
Prove no-loss or transfer: the target property is invariant under the symmetry or recoverable from the canonical case.
Prove invariant preservation once per canonical transition kind.
Show symmetry-breaking constraints are sound and do not strengthen the original theorem.

sources.title: Codex local math tactic card - Decompose And Symmetrize
Quanta Magazine - The Symmetry That Makes Solving Math Equations Easy

failure_modes: The target property is not invariant under the proposed symmetry.
Canonicalization drops data needed by the concrete theorem.
The proof adds symmetry-breaking assumptions but never transfers back to the original statement.
Repeated cases are hidden behind automation instead of replaced by a named quotient and transfer lemma.

tactics.name: Refine economic evidence into publication authority
tactics.summary: Preserve scoped donor proofs while requiring a release-selected verifier, exact public-journal binding, an opaque authority witness, and atomic publication before any settlement claim gains writer authority.
tactics.trigger: Use when a proved or contract-backed economic packet is being reused inside a new recursive proof or settlement publication path.
tactics.transform: Keep the donor claim at its existing evidence class, introduce an explicit verifier-owned opaque witness for the new authority boundary, bind profile, release, image, journal, receipt, effects, body, and state, and classify every missing guest, verifier, publisher, migration, or mount as a gap.
obligations: Name the exact scoped donor theorem or contract and preserve its original evidence class.
Require a release-selected verifier to accept the exact image id and canonical public journal before constructing authority.
Make the publisher consume only the verifier-owned opaque witness and recheck current profile, head, body, state, DA, and finality bindings.
Preserve a negative regression showing that structural, synthetic, fake, conditional, or development receipts cannot authorize publication.
Keep guest emission, cryptographic verification, durable publication, migration, route mounting, and writer retirement as explicit gaps until replayable evidence exists.
failure_modes: A local settlement theorem is relabeled as a global publication theorem.
A caller-constructible certificate or structural journal receives authority without cryptographic receipt verification.
The verifier checks a receipt against an image or journal different from the bytes committed by the publisher.
An in-memory or test-double path is described as durable or production-mounted authority.
